name: Crizotinib
drug_class: ALK, ROS1 and MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor
route_note: oral capsules twice daily; pellets/oral formulation for children

discovery.by: Pfizer La Jolla (J. Jean Cui and colleagues)
discovery.note: Designed as a MET inhibitor; activity against ALK became the focus after EML4-ALK fusions were discovered in lung cancer in 2007.

tagline: First ALK inhibitor, approved four years after ALK fusions were found in lung cancer
summary: Crizotinib is an oral inhibitor of the ALK, ROS1 and MET kinases. It was the first targeted therapy for ALK-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer and is also used for ROS1-positive lung cancer, ALK-positive anaplastic large-cell lymphoma and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumours.
mechanism: Chromosomal rearrangements such as EML4-ALK create constitutively active ALK fusion kinases that drive tumour growth. Crizotinib competitively binds the ATP pocket of ALK, ROS1 and MET, blocking downstream STAT3, PI3K–AKT and MAPK signalling.
Poor central nervous system penetration and ALK resistance mutations (e.g. L1196M, G1269A) limit durability, leading to next-generation ALK inhibitors.
uses: Relapsed or refractory ALK-positive anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (children and young adults)

history.title: EML4-ALK discovered
history.detail: Soda, Mano and colleagues report the EML4-ALK fusion in NSCLC (Nature).

history.title: Phase I results
history.detail: Kwak et al. (NEJM) report a 57% response rate in ALK-positive NSCLC.

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves crizotinib with the Vysis ALK FISH companion diagnostic.

history.title: ROS1
history.detail: FDA approves crizotinib for ROS1-positive NSCLC.

history.title: Lymphoma
history.detail: Approval for ALK-positive anaplastic large-cell lymphoma in young patients.

history.title: IMT
history.detail: Approval for ALK-positive inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour.

facts: The time from discovery of EML4-ALK to FDA approval of crizotinib was about four years.
